body:
CONTEXT. Spec section 7 point 1(b) (docs/specs/segmented-gate-manifest.md): when more than one committed segment declares the current branch and no local .lineage token disambiguates them, every keyed token-less write refuses (ambiguous) — fail-closed by design, since guessing which candidate to extend silently forks the lineage. The refusal is correct; what is missing is a supported remediation. Today an operator must hand-craft the gitignored .adlc/manifest.d/.lineage token file ({segment, ulid, branch}) to choose a candidate — undocumented, easy to get wrong (the ULID must match the segment's), and repeated per checkout. This state arises legitimately: two clones of the same branch each performing their first write before either sees the other's segment, both landing. Adversarial review of the dual-mode enable ticket flagged the missing remediation twice.

WORK. New `adlc gate-manifest adopt` subcommand (lib/adopt.mjs + bin wiring). Behavior: (a) dry-run by default, --write to apply, --json single-document output (repo conventions); (b) with no arguments, LIST the current branch's candidate segments (name, entry count, first/last timestamps, signed-entry count under the ambient... no — key must be an explicit parameter per the key contract: accept --key-file or reuse the bin's existing key resolution, matching how verify wires it) so the operator can choose; (c) `adopt <segment-name> --write` verifies the named segment: exists, grammar-valid name, declares the CURRENT branch in its first entry, chain intact, and — when a key is provided — authenticates like the writer's recovery gate (no tampered/unsigned-after-signed entries, at least one entry the key verifies); then writes the .lineage token {segment, ulid (from the filename), branch} atomically via the existing writeLineageToken; (d) refuses: a segment naming a DIFFERENT branch, a broken/unauthenticatable chain (with key), a repo that is not segmented, detached HEAD (no branch to bind the token to); (e) adopt never edits committed bytes — it writes only the local gitignored token, so it needs no ceremony and no rails.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA:
AC1 — list mode: in a fixture with two same-branch committed segments and no token, `gate-manifest adopt` exits 0 and lists both candidates. Verify: CLI test spawning the bin.
AC2 — adopt happy path: `adopt <name> --write` writes a token such that the next resolveOpenSegment takes the fast token path to the chosen segment and a subsequent append extends it; the other segment stays byte-identical. Verify: test asserting resolution and byte-identity.
AC3 — refusals: wrong-branch segment, chain-broken segment, keyed-but-unauthenticatable segment, non-segmented repo, and detached HEAD each exit 2 and write no token. Verify: table-driven tests.
AC4 — dry-run writes nothing; --json parses as exactly one document in every mode. Verify: tests.
AC5 — the ambiguous-write refusal error text in both resolvers points at `gate-manifest adopt` as the remediation. Verify: grep in both lib files plus the existing ambiguity tests still passing with the updated message.
AC6 — full suite green and mutation-gate clean: npm test; node scripts/mutation-gate.mjs origin/main --max 12.
AC7 — trust-root prosecution per repo standard: distinct-provider cross-model approve bound to the reviewed revision; adlc prosecute --base main exits 0.

PROCESS NOTES. (1) The spec edit (documenting adopt in section 7 point 1(b)) touches a frozen rail — expect the documented override path at merge. (2) Do not edit any existing ticket's body. (3) Mutation-gate rewrites prose in string literals — reword rather than pin. (4) Full suite before push.
title: gate-manifest adopt: operator command to disambiguate a branch with multiple committed segments by writing the local lineage token
